cards.explanation: The answer is to search for a young woman to care for him. The servants say, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him…” They aren't fiddling with the room or the furniture, friends. They're looking for a person to look after David.

The answer is chariots and fifty men to run ahead. Adonijah, one of David's sons, acquires “…chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.” That's a whole parade. And he's saying “I will be king!” at the time.
The answer is False. The text says “His father had never once reprimanded him…” David never once asked Adonijah why he acts this way. And in that same stretch, Adonijah is saying “I will be king!”

The answer is False. Adonijah confers with Joab and Abiathar the priest, who support him. But Nathan the prophet is named among those who “…would not join Adonijah.” Nathan isn't on his side, friends, and we're about to see what he does next.

The answer is Solomon. Solomon, another son of David, is the one left off. The text says Adonijah invited his royal brothers but “…did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.” Whatever the reason, I think the empty chair is the loudest thing at that party.
The answer is her life and Solomon's life, and it's serious. Nathan, the prophet, tells Bathsheba, “Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.” The stakes here are lives, not property.

The answer is True. Nathan tells Bathsheba to go to King David and remind him that he swore her son Solomon would reign after him and sit on his throne. Then she's to ask, “Why then has Adonijah become king?” It's a reminder with a question attached.
The word is “confirm.” Nathan says, “…I will come in after you and confirm your words.” He's not going to argue with her or change her story, friends. He plans to back her up.

The answer is True. Bathsheba tells David, “…the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.” She says the whole nation is waiting on his answer. That's a lot of eyes on one old king.

The answer is that they will be counted as criminals. Bathsheba tells David that when he rests with his fathers, “…I and my son Solomon will be counted as criminals.” She's saying plainly what's at stake if David stays silent.

The answer is “Did you say Adonijah will reign after you.” Nathan the prophet asks, “did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?” He puts it to David as a question. Then he goes on to tell David what Adonijah has done.

The answer is “Long live King Adonijah.” That's what Nathan says they're saying. They are eating and drinking before Adonijah and saying, “Long live King Adonijah!” That's a whole party cheering for Adonijah as king.

The answer is True. Nathan tells David that Adonijah has not invited “me your servant… nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon.” Zadok is a priest, and he's on the list of people left out. Nathan names himself on that list too.
The word is “today.” David swears, “I will carry out this very day exactly what I swore to you…” That's no maybe-later, friends. The king says it happens the same day.

The answer is David's own mule. David says, “Set my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to Gihon.” Riding the king's own mule is a loud way to show who's picked. It's David's mule, not a chariot like the ones Adonijah acquired.

The answer is False. David says Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint Solomon king at Gihon. Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, is one of the three men David calls in, and he answers, “Amen.” The anointing isn't his job.

The answer is even greater than David's. Benaiah asks that the LORD be with Solomon “…and make his throne even greater than that of my lord King David.” He says this to David's face, and he doesn't hold back.

The word is “oil.” Zadok the priest “…took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon.” It was oil taken from the tabernacle. Then they blew the ram's horn, and all the people proclaimed, “Long live King Solomon!”
The answer is that the earth splits from the sound. The people follow Solomon “…playing flutes and rejoicing with such a great joy that the earth was split by the sound.” That's one loud celebration.

The answer is False. Adonijah says Jonathan must be bringing good news, but Jonathan replies, “Not at all…” Then he says, “Our lord King David has made Solomon king.” That's not the news Adonijah said he expected.

The answer is seated on the royal throne. Jonathan says, “Moreover, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.” Solomon is not just anointed, friends, he's sitting on the throne. Jonathan has already told Adonijah that Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon king at Gihon.

The answer is True. Jonathan says the king “…has bowed in worship on his bed…” He tells Adonijah that David is saying, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel!” Then comes the rest of it: “Today He has provided one to sit on my throne, and my eyes have seen it.”
The answer is that they rise up in terror and scatter. The text says all the guests of Adonijah “…arose in terror and scattered.” The party ends fast.

The word is “altar.” Adonijah, “…in fear of Solomon, got up and went to take hold of the horns of the altar.” The text names his fear of Solomon outright. I think he grabs the altar because he's afraid, but that part is my guess.

The answer is not to put him to the sword. Adonijah says, “Let King Solomon first swear to me not to put his servant to the sword.” He asks for that oath first. He says it while he has taken hold of the horns of the altar.

The answer is whether he's a man of character. Solomon says, “If he is a man of character, not a single hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.” Solomon names two conditions with two outcomes. Whether Adonijah is a man of character or evil is found in him is what he points to.
The answer is “Go to your home.” Solomon says those words to Adonijah. Adonijah has just come down from the altar and bowed down before him. It's the one order Solomon gives him.
